description: Medieval pilgrimage routes carried people, badges, relics, and stories across enormous distances. This path follows a handful of objects and documents connected to the shrines, roads, and rituals that structured pilgrim travel.

Merchants, ledgers, and goods moved along dense commercial networks linking the Baltic, the North Sea, and the Mediterranean. This path traces some of the material and documentary traces left behind by that long-distance trade.

Envoys, legates, and letters travelled between courts to negotiate peace, alliances, and aid. This path follows a few of the people and objects caught up in the slow, difficult business of medieval diplomacy.
